summary: Iteration 48 — verified the full i18n sweep. All 57 non-EN locale files now contain exactly the 863 top-level keys defined in en.js (0 missing). The 9 recently-added keys (footer.legal.about, footer.legal.disclosure, home.plant_of_the_week.eyebrow, source.local.title/body/cta/tools_cta/searching_near, share_view.views) are present, non-empty, and actually translated (not English fallback) in all four low-resource languages (gd, cy, ga, mi). Backend companion-reasons regression from iter 47 still holds: /api/plants/tomato/companions?language=gd returns 'leumadair' for aphid and no English tokens; ga has no English pest leaks; /api/plants?language=ga returns 300+ plants with zero English pest-token leaks. 69/69 pytest tests pass in 8.94s (57 locale-completeness + 8 low-resource content + 4 backend regression).
critical_code_review_comments: scripts/i18n_audit.py uses a naive '^\s*"([^"]+)"\s*:' line-start regex (line 49) which misses concatenated keys — e.g. it under-counts every non-EN locale by 1–2 keys (home.plant_of_the_week.eyebrow, share_view.views). Recommend switching to the substring pattern '"([^"\\]+)"\s*:\s*"' used in the iter-48 test file to avoid future false-positive MISSING reports.

gd/source.local.cta still contains the English loanword 'nurseries' ('Lorg nurseries faisg orm'). Not an English-fallback failure per se (rest of sentence is Gaelic) but a native reviewer would expect 'lios-lusan' or 'plannt-lios'. Non-blocking; flag for a native pass.
mi/home.plant_of_the_week.eyebrow value ' tipu o te wiki' has a leading space and drops the definite article — expected 'Te tipu o te wiki'. Cosmetic; likely a translation-pipeline glitch.

58 locale files @ ~870 lines each are single monolithic dictionaries. They exceed the 700-line file-size threshold from code-review guidelines. Consider splitting by feature-namespace (nav.*, footer.*, plant.*, source.*) once the file count justifies the refactor.

translate_keys_for pipeline (scripts/i18n_sweep_fix.py) auto-writes without a diff-preview flag. For 57 files × 9 keys = 513 auto-writes, a --dry-run mode surfacing the proposed translations would catch cases like the mi/eyebrow leading-space bug before landing.

rca of the issue: Original user bug: English words leaking into translated UI copy across 58 locales. Root cause: a batch of ~9 recently-added keys (footer.legal.*, home.plant_of_the_week.*, source.local.*, share_view.views, share_patch.*) were only added to en.js and never propagated — the i18n runtime fell back to the English source at render time. Mitigation applied by E1 (this iter): scripts/i18n_audit.py + scripts/i18n_sweep_fix.py identified the missing keys and auto-injected translations via the existing translate_keys_for pipeline into all 57 non-EN locale files. Verification (this iter): 69/69 tests confirm 0 missing keys across 57 locales and 4/4 low-resource languages have properly translated (non-fallback) content for every recently-added key.
